metadata.title: SK Hynix Unveils $29 Billion US Listing as Shares Soar Over 800%

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
SK Hynix (HXSCL) shares jumped after the memory chipmaker laid out plans for a $29 billion US listing, a move analysts viewed as potentially boosting valuation by expanding capacity and opening easier access for foreign investors. The stock climbed nearly 12% in early Thursday trading before trimming gains to around 10%, while Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) also rallied after Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) posted a quarterly sales forecast that beat Wall Street expectations, helping push the Kospi Index up 6%.
SK Hynix is seeking 45.45 trillion won through the US listing after its Seoul-traded shares gained more than 800% over the past 12 months, lifting the company's market value above $1 trillion. The company expects its American depositary receipts to start trading on July 10, with proceeds intended for additional capacity and purchases of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, as global investors look for more direct exposure to a major high-bandwidth memory supplier tied to the AI supply chain.
At the proposed size, the ADR sale could rank among the top three first-time share sales ever, depending on exchange rates, and may rival Saudi Aramco's $29.4 billion IPO. Analysts said a liquid US listing could help SK Hynix sit closer to global semiconductor leaders such as TSMC (NYSE:TSM), though traders are watching whether the ADRs and Korean ordinary shares will be fully fungible, a key factor that could shape pricing gaps, arbitrage activity, and how much of any re-rating flows through each listing.
